# Adjudication Task — Chapter 243

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃243화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|혁무진은 하루하루 꿈 같은 나날을 보내고 있었다. 실제로 가끔 자신의 볼을 꼬집어 보기도 했다.
  6|
  7|‘무진아, 너 이렇게 행복해도 되는 거냐? 이거 꿈 아니야?’
  8|
  9|그럴 만도 했다.
 10|
 11|불과 십여 년 전만 해도 그는 단지 무림인들을 동경하는 소년에 불과했으니까.
 12|
 13|‘아니, 그렇게 멀리 갈 필요도 없나?’
 14|
 15|십 년 전이 아니라 이 년 전만 하더라도 현실이 시궁창 같다고 생각했다.
 16|
 17|업무 시간은 길고 지루했으며 무공은 제자리걸음이었다.
 18|
 19|그 와중에 가장 자주 마주치는 인간이 술에 떡이 된 망나니 삼공자라면, 부처가 아닌 이상 세상을 비관적으로 바라보기 마련이다.
 20|
 21|‘참고 참다가 한 방 질렀지.’
 22|
 23|삼공자의 턱에 주먹을 꽂아 넣은 그 날, 혁무진의 인생도 바뀌었다.
 24|
 25|수많은 전투, 죽음과 위기의 연속…….
 26|
 27|삼공자, 아니 조장은 마치 천하의 모든 위험을 끌어당기는 자철(磁鐵) 같았다.
 28|
 29|혁무진은 그와 함께 사방에서 날아드는 위험을 헤쳐 나갔고, 문득 정신을 차려보니 훌쩍 성장한 자신을 발견했다.
 30|
 31|
 32|
 33|‘오오, 힘이, 힘이 솟구친다!’
 34|
 35|‘……환자분. 이리 오세요. 지랄병이 도진 걸 보니 주먹 맞을 시간입니다.’
 36|
 37|
 38|
 39|빡! 빠바박!
 40|
 41|맞기도 참 많이 맞았다. 진태경 몰래 정화수를 떠 놓고 빈 적도 있다.
 42|
 43|
 44|
 45|‘제발, 제발 조장이 저 좀 못 때리게 해 주세요. 차라리 멀리 데려가 주세요.’
 46|
 47|
 48|
 49|그 소원이 통한 걸까?
 50|
 51|어느 날 진태경은 홀연히 떠났다.
 52|
 53|화왕과 함께 떠나는 그의 뒷모습을 보며 혁무진은 서운함과 해방감을 동시에 느꼈다.
 54|
 55|그리고 비로소 인생의 전성기가 찾아왔다.
 56|
 57|
 58|
 59|‘네가 혁무진이냐?’
 60|
 61|‘헉, 위팽 대협께서 어찌 저를…….’
 62|
 63|‘검을 뽑아라. 실력 한번 보자.’
 64|
 65|
 66|
 67|귀검 위팽이라는 절정 고수의 지도를 받게 되었고.
 68|
 69|
 70|
 71|‘진룡대(進龍隊)라고 하셨습니까?’
 72|
 73|‘그래. 본가의 최정예를 모은 곳이지. 내가 진룡대의 대주직을 맡게 되었다.’
 74|
 75|‘와! 진룡대! 감축드립니다!’
 76|
 77|‘짐 꾸려라.’
 78|
 79|‘예?’
 80|
 81|‘네가 부대주다. 주군의 명이니 한 치의 실수도 있어서는 안 될 것이다.’
 82|
 83|‘헉. 태원진가에 영원한 충성을 바치겠습니다. 존명존명!’
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|태원진가의 최정예라 할 수 있는 진룡대의 부대주가 되었다.
 88|
 89|일개 수문각주를 꿈꾸던 청년이, 불과 일이 년 사이에 가문 중진들과 어깨를 나란히 하는 실력자가 된 것이다.
 90|
 91|그야말로 꿈 같은 나날이었다.
 92|
 93|……적어도 촌각 전까지는.
 94|
 95|“너, 혁무진이지?”
 96|
 97|“……!”
 98|
 99|산발한 머리와 덥수룩한 수염. 누더기를 걸친 몸 좋은 거지의 입에서 흘러나온 말에 혁무진은 손발이 저려 왔다.
100|
101|더없이 익숙한 목소리. 어째서 단번에 알아보지 못했을까.
102|
103|어쩐지 이상하게 뒤통수가 근질거리더라니…….
104|
105|‘뭐가 어디서부터 잘못된 거지?’
106|
107|이번 하남행에 진위경의 수행원 자격으로 따라오게 된 것?
108|
109|아니면 아버지의 부탁을 받아 혁가 포목점 하남 지점을 점검하게 된 것?
110|
111|모르겠다. 지금 그가 확신할 수 있는 건 한 가지뿐이었다.
112|
113|‘좆 됐다.’
114|
115|식은땀이 등허리를 타고 미끄러짐과 동시에, 하남행을 지옥행으로 만들어 버리는 한마디가 들려왔다.
116|
117|“삼 초 준다. 대가리 박아.”
118|
119|싫다고 외치는 머리와는 달리 몸은 솔직했다.
120|
121|태원진가의 떠오르는 실력자이자, 가문 최정예인 진룡대의 부대주 혁무진은 우렁찬 외침과 함께 대가리를 박았다.
122|
123|“조오오온며여어어엉!”
124|
125|쿵!
126|
127|
128|
129|* * *
130|
131|
132|
133|하얀 돌담과 그 안으로 보이는 대여섯 개의 지붕들.
134|
135|현재 태원진가가 머무르고 있다는 커다란 장원이 점점 가까워지기 시작한다.
136|
137|“여기 맞아?”
138|
139|“……예.”
140|
141|혁무진이 반쯤 죽어 가는 목소리로 대답했다. 멋들어지던 무복은 너덜거렸고, 눈 한쪽은 푸르뎅뎅하게 멍이 들어 있었다.
142|
143|한 식경 전쯤 녀석이 했던 말을 빌리자면, 이게 바로 만용의 대가다.
144|
145|“오. 숙소 좋은 곳으로 잡았네. 요즘 잘나가나 봐?”
146|
147|일 년 사이 변화한 것은 나뿐만이 아니다. 혁무진도, 태원진가의 위상도 달라졌다.
148|
149|성라대연이 코앞으로 다가온 시점에 이렇게 큰 장원 하나를 통째로 빌린 것만 봐도 충분히 짐작할 수 있었다.
150|
151|“앞장서, 인마.”
152|
153|“으헉! 아픕니다, 아픕니다!”
154|
155|“아프라고 때리는 거야, 인마.”
156|
157|나는 녀석의 엉덩이를 뻥뻥 걷어차며 걸었다.
158|
159|장원 앞에서 칼 같은 자세로 경계를 취하던 태원진가의 무인 둘이 상관을 발견하고 입을 딱 벌렸다.
160|
161|“헉!”
162|
163|“부대주님!”
164|
165|혁무진이 슬쩍 시선을 회피하며 헛기침을 했다.
166|
167|“커흠. 근무 잘 서고 있었느냐? 이분은…….”
168|
169|스릉, 차차창!
170|
171|“네 이놈!”
172|
173|“감히 우리 부대주님을!”
174|
175|진룡대인지 뭔지 하는 신설 부대의 부대주라더니, 수하들 사이에서 제법 인망이 있는 모양이다.
176|
177|나는 검을 들이대는 진룡대원들을 보며 허허 웃었다.
178|
179|“검 내려요. 저 태원진가 관계잡니다.”
180|
181|“부대주님, 괜찮으십니까!”
182|
183|“이 거지 같은 놈이 어디서 헛소리를 하느냐!”
184|
185|부하들의 반응에 혁무진이 참담한 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
186|
187|“거지 같은 놈이 아니라 삼공자님이시다.”
188|
189|“예?”
190|
191|“아니, 아무리 봐도 거진데…….”
192|
193|한 번은 참겠는데, 두 번째는 아니다.
194|
195|내 표정 변화를 눈치챈 혁무진이 침울한 목소리로 입을 열었다.
196|
197|“호철아.”
198|
199|호철이라 불린 대원이 냉큼 대답했다.
200|
201|“예, 부대주님.”
202|
203|“대가리 박아라.”
204|
205|“…….”
206|
207|그렇지. 이 정도는 해 줘야 오른팔이지.
208|
209|땅과의 대화를 나누게 된 호철이를 뒤로하고 장원으로 발을 디뎠다. 그리고 거의 동시에 마당을 거닐고 있던 한 사람과 맞닥트렸다.
210|
211|“……!”
212|
213|“……!”
214|
215|격동하는 눈동자.
216|
217|일 년이 아니라 십 년이 지나도 그는 나를 알아볼 것이다. 아무리 행색이 엉망이어도 마찬가지다.
218|
219|핏줄이란, 형제란 그런 존재니까.
220|
221|“이런, 누군가 했더니.”
222|
223|석상처럼 굳은 채 나를 바라보던 거구의 사내. 진위경의 만면에 환한 미소가 맺힌다.
224|
225|나를 향해 성큼성큼 다가온 그가 입을 열었다.
226|
227|“개방에서 오신 분입니까?”
228|
229|“…….”
230|
231|형제는 니미.
232|
233|
234|
235|* * *
236|
237|
238|
239|“사실 한눈에 알아봤다.”
240|
241|“장난치십니까?”
242|
243|“정말이다. 설마하니 내가 막내 너를 못 알아봤을까!”
244|
245|“제가 빙다리 핫바지로 보이세요?”
246|
247|어디서 밑장을 빼. 개방에서 무슨 직책을 맡고 있는지 물어보기까지 했으면서.
248|
249|내 반응에 안절부절못하던 진위경이 혁무진에게 물었다.
250|
251|“이보게. 혁 부대주. 내가 아까 전음을 보내지 않았나. 못 알아본 척 장난을 칠 테니 장단 맞추라고.”
252|
253|“어, 그게 말입니다.”
254|
255|“내 말이 맞지? 응?”
256|
257|혁무진이 이마를 찡그렸다.
258|
259|“아야. 소가주님. 갑자기 왜 발을 밟으십니까?”
260|
261|“혀, 혁 부대주!”
262|
263|“아악. 아픕니다!”
264|
265|“…….”
266|
267|애쓴다. 애써.
268|
269|굳이 보지 않아도 탁자 아래에서 어떤 일이 벌어지고 있는지는 훤히 알고 있다.
270|
271|그들의 모습을 지켜보던 나는 문득 실소를 흘렸다.
272|
273|‘여전하구나.’
274|
275|진위경과 혁무진.
276|
277|내가 알던 두 사람이 맞다. 일 년 사이 많은 일을 겪었는지 전보다 관록과 여유가 붙었지만 알맹이는 여전했다.
278|
279|변하지 않았다는 것. 그것만으로도 충분하다.
280|
281|‘다른 사람들은 어떻게 됐으려나?’
282|
283|궁금증은 얼마 지나지 않아 풀렸다.
284|
285|진위경은 내가 떠난 직후부터 무슨 일이 있었는지 소상히 설명해 주었고, 그 안에 아직 해후하지 못한 이들의 행적이 들어 있었다.
286|
287|여전히 항산검문의 성세를 되찾기 위해 고군분투하는 이소월, 비교적 황량하던 산서 북부 지역에 유흥 도시를 세우고 있는 월화.
288|
289|그리고…….
290|
291|“청풍이 실종됐다고요?”
292|
293|“그래. 네가 떠나고 얼마 되지 않아 매화삼절과 함께 화산파로 향했는데, 도중에 도망쳤다더구나.”
294|
295|그건 실종이 아니라 탈주 아니냐.
296|
297|이어지는 이야기를 들어 보니 청풍이 사라진 후 한바탕 난리가 났던 모양이다.
298|
299|화산파에서 끗발 좀 날리는 장로가 찾아와 직접 부탁까지 했단다. 청풍 새끼 보면 연락 좀 해 달라고.
300|
301|“문파 제일의 어른과 후기지수가 차례대로 사라졌으니 그럴 만도 하지. 보는 내가 가슴이 미어지더라.”
302|
303|검성이나 청풍이나, 이쯤 되면 진짜 혈연관계가 아닌지 의심해 봐야 하는 게 아닌가 싶다.
304|
305|“화산파도 참 잘 굴러가네요.”
306|
307|“그래도 본가보다는 낫지.”
308|
309|“왜요. 북부 마적들도 쓸어 버리고 승승장구하는 중 아니에요? 이 정도면 나름 잘 하고 있는 것 같은데.”
310|
311|진위경이 우울한 얼굴로 고개를 저었다.
312|
313|“화산파는 그나마 문주에 제자들이라도 많지. 우리는 가주 자리가 공석이다.”
314|
315|“아.”
316|
317|“그래서인지 남 일 같지 않더구나. 앞으로 서로 도와주기로 했다. 힘든 문파끼리 돕고 살아야지.”
318|
319|이걸 이렇게 상부상조하네.
320|
321|나는 몇 년째 행방이 묘연한 가주라는 인간을 생각하다가 이내 머릿속에서 지워 버렸다.
322|
323|이곳 무림에서는 내 아버지겠지만 얼굴 한 번 못 본, 말 그대로 생판 남이다.
324|
325|혈육의 정은 물론이고 보고 싶은 마음도 없었다.
326|
327|‘보면 보는 거고. 아니면 말고.’
328|
329|오히려 틈만 나면 서로 으르렁거리던 진무경에게 훨씬 마음이 쓰였다.
330|
331|“그러고 보니 둘째 형은요. 어디 갔습니까?”
332|
333|시간이 꽤 흘렀음에도 나타나지 않는다.
334|
335|위팽은 진위경을 대신해서 태원 진가를 지키고 있다고 쳐도, 진무경은 왔을 것이 분명한데…….
336|
337|“폐관 수련 중이다.”
338|
339|“어? 또요?”
340|
341|“그것보다는 아직까지, 라는 말이 더 옳겠지.”
342|
343|“……설마 그 후로 쭉?”
344|
345|고개를 끄덕이는 진위경의 모습에 기가 찼다.
346|
347|무협 소설에서야 개나 소나 수십 년을 폐관 수련이니, 면벽 수련을 하니 하지만, 실제로 해 보면 불가능에 가깝다는 사실을 알게 된다.
348|
349|일 년만 되어도 엄청난 정신력이 아니고서야 버틸 수 없다.
350|
351|‘진무경이 폐관에 들어간 게 언제쯤이었지?’
352|
353|청풍과의 비무에서 패배한 직후니까, 지금까지의 시간으로는 일 년 하고도 육 개월은 될 것이다.

“……”

“Oh.”

“He’s in closed-door training.”

[P158]
“Huh? Again?”

[P159]
“Still would be more accurate.”

[P160]

[P161]

[P162]
In martial-arts novels, everyone and his dog spent decades in closed-door training or meditating before a wall, but anyone who actually tried it would quickly realize it was nearly impossible.

[P163]
Even a single year would be unbearable without extraordinary mental fortitude.

[P164]
*When did Jin Mukyung enter closed-door training?*

[P165]
It had been right after he lost his duel with Cheongpung, which meant he had been in there for a year and six months by now.

[P166]
For all that time, he had not taken a single step out of the dark training hall. He had devoted himself to ceaseless training, surviving on water and fasting pills for all three meals.

[P167]
“Could he have been in there so long that he lost track of the date? Maybe he didn’t know about the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

[P168]
“I went to see Mukyung before we left and told him about it. I asked if he wanted to come with us.”

[P172]
Great Completion…

[P173]
To Jin Mukyung, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a fruit within easy reach.

[P174]
He was already one of the foremost young prodigies in the Central Plains. If he entered, he could prove his martial arts and win even greater fame.

[P175]
But Jin Mukyung had chosen his martial arts over that sweet fruit.

[P176]
*He’s an incredible bastard.*

[P177]
While everyone else reached for the fruit and scrambled up the tree, Jin Mukyung had turned his back on it and devoted himself to training.

[P178]
And one day, when his training was complete, he would possess not the fruit, but the tree itself.

[P179]
A tree laden with fruit.

[P180]
*Yeah. That’s a true martial artist.*

[P181]
I respected his choice. I didn’t know what awaited Jin Mukyung at the end of the path he had chosen, but I knew he was headed in the right direction.

[P182]
That was enough.

[P183]
I murmured with a sigh.

[P184]
“So that’s how it turned out.”

[P185]
“Are you disappointed?”

[P186]
“A little. I was hoping the three of us would get together again.”

[P187]
“Even without those two, the world is full of exceptional masters. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are right there, aren’t they?”

[P188]
“I guess.”

At my lukewarm response, Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

[P190]
“Then I’ll have to turn that disappointment into joy.”

[P191]
“Pardon?”

[P192]

[P193]
A present? As I stared at him in confusion, Hyuk Mujin rose from his chair.

[P194]
A short while later, he returned carrying something long and tightly wrapped in thick cloth.

[P195]
“Do you know what it is?”

[P196]
Of course I did. The moment I saw it, my heart began to pound and my fingertips twitched.

[P197]
It was instinct.

[P198]
Not Jin Taekyung’s instinct, but a spearman’s.

[P199]
“This is…”

[P200]
“Fifteen days ago, Elder Jang Taebo handed this to me and said something.”

[P201]
Shrrk.

[P202]
As Hyuk Mujin peeled away the cloth, Jin Wikyung’s voice rang in my ears.

[P203]
“He said he finally understood how Gan Jiang and Mo Ye must have felt.”[^1]

[P204]
Vrrrrm.

[P205]
The spear let out a low hum.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

“The sect’s most senior elder and its young prodigy vanished one after another. Their reaction was understandable. Just watching them made my heart ache.”

[P140]
The Sword Saint and Cheongpung… At this point, shouldn’t I start wondering whether they were actually related by blood?

[P141]
“Huashan is really thriving.”

[P142]
“It’s still doing better than our family.”

[P143]
“Why? Didn’t we wipe out the mounted bandits in the north? Aren’t we on a roll? From where I’m standing, the family seems to be doing pretty well.”

[P144]
Jin Wikyung shook his head gloomily.

[P145]
“Huashan at least has a Sect Leader and plenty of disciples. Our Family Head’s seat is vacant.”

[P146]
“Oh.”

[P147]
“Perhaps that’s why their situation didn’t feel like someone else’s problem. We agreed to help each other from now on. Struggling martial factions have to support one another.”

[P148]
So that was how they ended up helping each other out.

[P149]
I thought of the man who had been missing for years—the Family Head—then promptly erased him from my mind.

[P150]
In this Murim, he might be my father, but I had never even seen his face. He was a complete stranger.

[P151]
I felt no familial affection for him, much less any desire to see him.

[P152]
*If I see him, I see him. If not, whatever.*

[P153]
I was far more concerned about Jin Mukyung, whom I’d traded snarls with every chance we got.

[P154]
“Come to think of it, where’s Second Hyung? Did he go somewhere?”

[P155]
Quite a bit of time had passed, but he still hadn’t appeared.

[P156]
Wipeng might have stayed behind to guard the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Jin Wikyung’s absence, but Jin Mukyung should definitely have come…

[P157]
“He’s in closed-door training.”

[P158]
“Huh? Again?”

[P159]
“Still would be more accurate.”

[P160]
“…You mean he’s been in there this whole time?”

[P161]
I was dumbfounded when Jin Wikyung nodded.

[P162]
In martial-arts novels, everyone and his dog spent decades in closed-door training or meditating before a wall, but anyone who actually tried it would quickly realize it was nearly impossible.

[P163]
Even a single year would be unbearable without extraordinary mental fortitude.

[P164]
*When did Jin Mukyung enter closed-door training?*

[P165]
It had been right after he lost his duel with Cheongpung, which meant he had been in there for a year and six months by now.

[P166]
For all that time, he had not taken a single step out of the dark training hall. He had devoted himself to ceaseless training, surviving on water and fasting pills for all three meals.

[P167]
“Could he have been in there so long that he lost track of the date? Maybe he didn’t know about the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

[P168]
“I went to see Mukyung before we left and told him about it. I asked if he wanted to come with us.”

[P169]
I didn’t need to hear his answer. Jin Mukyung’s absence told me everything.

[P170]
Jin Wikyung continued quietly.

[P171]
“He said he wouldn’t leave until he achieved Great Completion. He asked me to tell you that.”

[P172]
Great Completion…

[P173]
To Jin Mukyung, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a fruit within easy reach.

[P174]
He was already one of the foremost young prodigies in the Central Plains. If he entered, he could prove his martial arts and win even greater fame.

[P175]
But Jin Mukyung had chosen his martial arts over that sweet fruit.

[P176]
*He’s an incredible bastard.*

[P177]
While everyone else reached for the fruit and scrambled up the tree, Jin Mukyung had turned his back on it and devoted himself to training.

[P178]
And one day, when his training was complete, he would possess not the fruit, but the tree itself.

[P179]
A tree laden with fruit.

[P180]
*Yeah. That’s a true martial artist.*

[P181]
I respected his choice. I didn’t know what awaited Jin Mukyung at the end of the path he had chosen, but I knew he was headed in the right direction.

[P182]
That was enough.

[P183]
I murmured with a sigh.

[P184]
“So that’s how it turned out.”

[P185]
“Are you disappointed?”

[P186]
“A little. I was hoping the three of us would get together again.”

[P187]
“Even without those two, the world is full of exceptional masters. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are right there, aren’t they?”

[P188]
“I guess.”

[P189]
At my lukewarm response, Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.

[P190]
“Then I’ll have to turn that disappointment into joy.”

[P191]
“Pardon?”

[P192]
“I brought you a present.”

[P193]
A present? As I stared at him in confusion, Hyuk Mujin rose from his chair.

[P194]
A short while later, he returned carrying something long and tightly wrapped in thick cloth.

[P195]
“Do you know what it is?”

[P196]
Of course I did. The moment I saw it, my heart began to pound and my fingertips twitched.

[P197]
It was instinct.

[P198]
Not Jin Taekyung’s instinct, but a spearman’s.

[P199]
“This is…”

[P200]
“Fifteen days ago, Elder Jang Taebo handed this to me and said something.”

[P201]
Shrrk.

[P202]
As Hyuk Mujin peeled away the cloth, Jin Wikyung’s voice rang in my ears.

[P203]
“He said he finally understood how Gan Jiang and Mo Ye must have felt.”[^1]

[P204]
Vrrrrm.

[P205]
The spear let out a low hum.

[P206]
[^1]: Gan Jiang and Mo Ye are a legendary husband-and-wife pair of swordsmiths from Chinese lore.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
